name: Ambasada Kultury
overview: Initiative of Belarusian culture workers and activists in exile, with no gallery of its own. It calls itself a network of "non-localized culture ambassadors" (stated by the initiative). CEC ArtsLink lists it as founded in Minsk and now based in Berlin. The initiative's own PerspAKTIV page tags it "Belarus/Lithuania".

Founded in 2021 by Valentina Kiselyova and Anna Chistoserdova (spellings as on the Berlin Art Week and Kalektar pages), who earlier ran the Podzemka gallery in Minsk (2004 to 2009) and the contemporary art gallery Ў (2009 to 2020) (Berlin Art Week; CEC ArtsLink).

Ў gallery was dissolved on 29 October 2020. Wikipedia says that year its co-owner Aliaksandr Vasilievič was described as a political prisoner, and that he and his partners divested their stakes in the gallery and its bar. Kiselyova left Belarus in June 2021 and has lived and worked in Berlin and Poznań since (Kalektar).
funding_verdict: Ambasada Kultury: mainly public: German Federal Foreign Office support for the PerspAKTIV residencies

name: Künstlerhaus Bethanien
overview: Residency house and exhibition venue in Kreuzberg, Berlin. Its International Studio Programme brings around 40 artists a year from across the world, who show work in exhibitions, open studios and events (Bethanien).
Founded in 1974 by Dr. Michael Haerdter in a former deaconess hospital on Mariannenplatz, after a plan to demolish the abandoned hospital was halted by protest (Bethanien history page).
The name refers to the biblical town associated with Lazarus (Bethanien history page).
funding_verdict: Künstlerhaus Bethanien: institutionally funded by the Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, with 32 named partner organisations

press_items.title: Amelia Abraham, "An Afrofuturism exhibition is being criticised for excluding black artists" (31 July 2019)

name: E-WERK Luckenwalde
overview: Contemporary art centre in a former brown coal power station at Rudolf-Breitscheid-Strasse 73, Luckenwalde, Brandenburg, about 50 km (40 minutes by train) south of Berlin (UBS Art; Reiseland Brandenburg).

Artist Pablo Wendel founded the non-profit Performance Electrics in 2012. He and curator Helen Turner found the derelict station in 2017, and Performance Electrics took it over that year. The centre opened with Power Night on 14 September 2019 (UBS Art; Studio International; The Art Newspaper).
Earlier use: a coal power plant built in 1913 that supplied Luckenwalde for over 60 years and stopped around 1989 (Reiseland Brandenburg).
funding_verdict: E-WERK Luckenwalde: mixed public and self-earned: German federal and state culture money plus electricity sales that fund the art programme

name: Die Neue Sammlung - The Design Museum
overview: Design museum in the Pinakothek der Moderne at Barer Straße 40 in the Maxvorstadt district of Munich. It describes itself as one of the world's oldest and most significant museums for applied art and design from the 20th and 21st centuries (stated by the space).

Its origins lie in the founding of the Deutscher Werkbund in Munich in 1907, when a "Moderne Vorbildersammlung" was started. It became a state museum of the Free State of Bavaria in 1925 and has used the name Die Neue Sammlung since 1929 (German Wikipedia).
From 1925 to 2002 it was housed in the western garden wing of the Bayerisches Nationalmuseum. It opened in the Pinakothek der Moderne in September 2002 (German Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Die Neue Sammlung: state museum of the Free State of Bavaria, with a friends' association and a partner company

name: Akademie Schloss Solitude
overview: Residency academy for artists and researchers in the late-Baroque Schloss Solitude, on a hill overlooking Stuttgart. A project space is on Römerstrasse in the city centre.

Opened in 1990 as a foundation under public law, "financially supported by the German province of Baden-Württemberg" (the Akademie's about page). It has hosted about 1,700 young artists from more than 120 countries (the Akademie's own count; German Wikipedia gives more than 1,400 fellows).
Named for the castle it occupies. Directors: Jean-Baptiste Joly (founding director until 2018), Elke aus dem Moore (until 2022), and Anne Fleckstein since February 2024 (German Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Akademie Schloss Solitude: mainly public: the state of Baden-Württemberg
wider_context: On 30 October 2023 the Akademie published a statement on the situation in the Middle East that condemned the Hamas attack on Israel, especially its targeting of civilians, and expressed solidarity with those who lost family and friends in Israel, Gaza and the other Palestinian territories. The statement does not mention an open letter or a ministry (the Akademie's statement).

Unverified: fellows circulated a statement with "antiisraelischen Positionen" in October 2023, and a review by Science Minister Petra Olschowski had no consequences for the fellows, from German Wikipedia, which cites the Stuttgarter Zeitung. The Stuttgarter Zeitung piece was not read and the statement's text was not found; the Akademie's own statement and Policy of Respect do not mention it.

Policy of Respect: the Akademie has a published policy for staff, fellows, jury members, partners, guests and service providers. It names forms of discrimination including antisemitism and anti-Muslim racism, and sets sanctions from formal warnings to termination of fellowships and reports to the police.

name: Chale Wote Street Art Festival
overview: Annual street art festival in Accra, organised by ACCRA [dot] ALT. Mantse Aryeequaye and Sionne Neely established the festival in 2011 (Nataal, 2018).

Began as a conversation: in April 2011 Aryeequaye proposed a street art festival at an Accra [dot] Alt talk party, and the first festival in July 2011 drew about 1,000 people (TRUE Africa, Bianca Manu, 2015 interview).

Held in Jamestown, which Aryeequaye called the oldest part of Accra, with colonial and pre-colonial history (TRUE Africa). In 2023 programming was limited to the Osu municipality, from 21 to 27 August at Black Star Square, with no activities in James Town (festival press release).
funding_verdict: Chale Wote Street Art Festival: self-funded by the organisers, with State institutions and private partners from 2023

name: National Museum of Ghana
overview: Ghana's national museum at 2 Barnes Road, Adabraka, Accra.
Established on 5 March 1957 as part of the celebrations of independence from colonial rule.
It closed in 2015 for renovation and restoration and reopened in June 2022 after seven years; President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo spoke at the commissioning.
funding_verdict: National Museum of Ghana: mainly public: the Ghana Museums and Monuments Board and the Government of Ghana

press_items.title: Jon Olav Hove, "Ghana's National Museum: superb restoration but painful stories remain untold" (2022)

name: Nubuke Foundation
overview: Visual art and cultural institution at 7 Lome Close, East Legon, Accra, described as a creative hub for contemporary art, heritage and culture in Ghana (MyJoyOnline, Odile Tevie, 2 August 2026).

Established in April 2006 by Odile Tevie, Kofi Tutu Agyare and Kofi Setordji (MyJoyOnline, 2 August 2026). Its first project was a photographic book, Ghana: A Portrait, released before Ghana's 50th independence anniversary. Tevie is director and Setordji artistic director (Daily Graphic, 15 October 2016).
Programmes include exhibitions, poetry and drama evenings and workshops, and the Woori Festival, which runs every two years, with the next edition in 2027 (foundation website).
funding_verdict: Nubuke Foundation: privately founded, with project funding from the EU and the British Council

name: NEON
overview: Non-profit contemporary art organisation in Athens that "does not restrict itself to just one space" (NEON website). Wikipedia describes projects on archaeological sites and in partner venues.

Founded in 2013 by collector and entrepreneur Dimitris Daskalopoulos (NEON website, Wikipedia), and directed by Elina Kountouri (Wikipedia). NEON's April 2026 post is titled "NEON 2012 to 2026 | 14 years of contemporary art".

NEON's site describes free exhibitions in public and private places in Athens and Greece, scholarships and grants for artists, educational programmes, live events and partnerships with cultural institutions.
funding_verdict: NEON: private non-profit: collector Dimitris Daskalopoulos, its founder, is the named funder of its projects

name: MOMus
overview: MOMus, the Metropolitan Organisation of Museums of Visual Arts of Thessaloniki, runs five institutions: the Museum of Modern Art with the Costakis Collection, the Museum of Contemporary Art, the Thessaloniki Museum of Photography and the Experimental Center for the Arts in Thessaloniki, and the Alex Mylona Museum in Athens. The Hamza Bey Mosque "Alkazar" is also listed among its venues (MOMus website).
Four museums in Thessaloniki and one in Athens joined forces in November 2018 to form MOMus (MOMus website).

In April 2017 the Culture Minister Lydia Koniordou announced the merger of the State Museum of Contemporary Art and the Macedonian Museum of Contemporary Art as the first step (Greek Travel Pages, 21 April 2017).
funding_verdict: MOMus: mainly public: the Greek Ministry of Culture and the EU Recovery Fund

name: Katuaq Greenland Cultural Centre
overview: Cultural centre at Imaneq 21 in Nuuk, Greenland's capital, used for concerts, exhibitions, conferences and as a cinema (Wikipedia; the centre's website).

Built as a joint project of the Greenland Home Rule Government, the Nuuk Municipal Council and the Nordic Council of Ministers. Construction ran from 1994 to 1997 and it opened on 15 February 1997 (Wikipedia).
Danish name: Grønlands Kulturhus.
funding_verdict: Katuaq: mainly public: the Greenland Self-Government and Kommuneqarfik Sermersooq, with bank and airline sponsors

name: Museo Ixchel del Traje Indígena
overview: Museum of Guatemalan Indigenous textiles and dress, in the Centro Cultural UFM on the Universidad Francisco Marroquín campus, at the end of 6th Street, Zone 10, Guatemala City (museum site; Wikipedia).

It grew from a committee of the Tikal Association that decided in the early 1970s to document Maya textile traditions. Carmen Pettersen painted watercolours of the costumes and her husband Leon Lind Pettersen published them, with the proceeds meant to fund a museum. The museum opened in 1976 in a rented house in Guatemala City's hotel district (Holly Nottebohm, Harvard DRCLAS ReVista, 4 December 2010).

In 1993, after consulting textile curators at the Metropolitan Museum of New York, it moved into a new building on the UFM campus (DRCLAS). Wikipedia lists the architects as Victor Cohen, Peter Giesemann, Augusto de León Fajardo, Adolfo Lau and William Pemüeller, and says the exterior looks like a woven textile pattern.
funding_verdict: Museo Ixchel del Traje Indígena: small private museum supported by memberships, a US friends charity and local companies

name: Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida (MUNAM)
overview: National modern art museum in Salón 6 of La Aurora, zone 13, Guatemala City. It is a national monument (Agencia Guatemalteca de Noticias, AGN, June 2023).

Its roots are the Museo Nacional de Historia y Bellas Artes, opened on 10 November 1934 in the former El Calvario temple in zone 1. The temple was demolished in 1947, the collections moved to La Aurora, and the museum took over Salón 6 there in 1968 (Prensa Comunitaria).
Renamed Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno de Guatemala in 1975, and named after the artist Carlos Mérida in 1999 by ministerial agreement 428-99 (Prensa Comunitaria).
funding_verdict: Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida: mainly public: the Ministerio de Cultura y Deportes (state budget)

name: Museo Popol Vuh
overview: Archaeology and colonial art museum on the campus of Universidad Francisco Marroquín (UFM) in Zone 10, Guatemala City (Wikipedia).
Founded in 1977 by Jorge and Ella Castillo from their private collection. In 1978 they donated it to UFM to establish the museum (Brenda Larios, Agencia Guatemalteca de Noticias, 30 May 2021).
Named for the Popol Vuh, the book written soon after the Spanish conquest that narrates the myths and pre-Columbian history of the K'iche' people (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Museo Popol Vuh: university museum supported by its own resources and corporate donors

name: Musée National de Guinée (Sandervalia)
overview: Guinea's national museum, in the Sandervalia quarter of Kaloum, Conakry, near Ignace Deen Hospital (Wikipedia).

Founded in 1960 to hold examples of traditional arts, linked to a state policy promoting traditional folklore (Wikipedia). Guinéenews (Mady Bangoura, 6 April 2023) says a sanitation campaign under Sékou Touré led to the site being designated the national museum.

Named for the French explorer Aimé Olivier de Sanderval, who settled on the site. His house, built around 1897, and his forge remain, and the house was classified as a historic monument in 1960 (Guinéenews).
funding_verdict: Musée National de Guinée: state museum: rebuilding financed by a concessional loan from the French Development Agency (AFD)

name: FOKAL
overview: Haitian national foundation working in education, human rights, civic engagement, arts and culture and sustainable development, based at 143 Avenue Christophe, Port-au-Prince (FOKAL).

Name in full: Fondation Connaissance et Liberté / Fondasyon Konesans Ak Libète, the Foundation for Knowledge and Liberty. In January 1995 Aryeh Neier, then president of the Open Society Institute, contacted Michèle Duvivier Pierre-Louis to create it. The foundation was created in April 1995, she appointed seven volunteers as the first board in July 1995 and it received public utility status in 2000 (FOKAL).

Pierre-Louis was its executive director from 1995 to 2008 and a FOKAL post of 29 May 2025 calls her its president. FOKAL's history page lists Maxime D. Charles as board president since January 2015. Lorraine Mangonès is executive director (FOKAL annual report 2024).
funding_verdict: FOKAL: foundation-funded: Open Society Foundations until 2024, now W.K. Kellogg Foundation, Ford Foundation, Citi-CAF, the European Union, the French Development Agency and the diaspora fund Ayiti Demen

name: Museo para la Identidad Nacional (MIN)
overview: History and culture museum in the former Palacio de los Ministerios in Barrio Abajo, in the historic centre of Tegucigalpa (museum website).
Opened on 19 January 2006 under President Ricardo Maduro (El Heraldo, 2019); the museum says Maduro conceived the project after visiting the Panama Canal Museum (museum website).

Building: Marco Aurelio Soto laid the first stone in 1882; it first housed the city's General Hospital, which moved out in May 1926, then several ministries; it was restored from late 2004 and is listed as a national monument by the Honduran Institute of Anthropology and History (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo para la Identidad Nacional: private non-profit foundation with an endowment and corporate patrons, set up under a state project

name: CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile)
overview: Non-profit textile art centre on the 2nd floor of The Mills, 45 Pak Tin Par Street, Tsuen Wan, in the former Nan Fung Cotton Mills. Wikipedia places it in Unit 6 (CHAT website, Wikipedia).
Nan Fung Cotton Mills was founded in 1954 by Chen Din Hwa, who also founded Nan Fung Group. Units 4 to 6 stopped spinning in 2008 and became warehouses (Wikipedia, citing Ming Pao).
Nan Fung announced the revitalisation of the mills in 2014. CHAT opened on 16 March 2019 with the inaugural exhibition "Unfolding: Fabric of Our Life" (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: CHAT: private: a property group and a family foundation. Nan Fung Group is main donor and the D. H. Chen Foundation is founding donor
wider_context: Wikipedia (The Mills, Hong Kong), citing HK01 and Ming Pao, reports that on 6 May 2020 a photo posted by then-Chief Executive Carrie Lam led to an HK01 reporter finding a workshop making anti-epidemic masks on the 4th floor of the mill complex. Staff and security guards expelled the reporter and the room was sealed with plywood.

Wikipedia, citing Ming Pao of 17 May 2020, says the 2018 revitalisation deed did not allow "industrial purposes" in Units 4 and 5, which Nan Fung Cotton Mills (No. 2) Co. leased to Nan Fung Workshop Incubation Center Ltd. It reports the lawyer Tse Tin Leung saying the site is limited to small samples, and questioning whether large-scale production breaches the deed.
The workshop was in the mill complex that Nan Fung Group developed, and Nan Fung Group is CHAT's main donor. CHAT is in Unit 6.

name: Ludwig Museum Budapest
overview: Museum of contemporary art in the wing of the Müpa Budapest (formerly the Palace of Arts) facing the Danube, with 3,300 square metres of exhibition space (Ludwig Museum).

Founded by the German collectors Peter and Irene Ludwig: the founding contract was signed on 21 March 1989, and the Ludwig Foundation gave 70 works to the Hungarian state and lent others on long-term deposit (Ludwig Museum).
The first permanent exhibition opened on 4 June 1991 in Building A of the Buda Castle Palace; it moved to the Müpa in 2005 (Ludwig Museum).
funding_verdict: Ludwig Museum Budapest: public: a central government body, with the Ludwig Foundation, companies and foreign bodies paying for acquisitions and shows
wider_context: 2013: more than 30 artists occupied the museum from 9 to 22 May over the director tender; they said the Ludwig Foundation backed the incumbent Barnabás Bencsik against Fabényi, whom they called "Fidesz-backed" (ArtLeaks).
2019: the museum left Brückner's mural "Here and Now" out of its 30th anniversary show; Emerging Europe cites no government instruction.

2025: MNB-Ingatlan Kft. paid the museum HUF 21 million under a cooperation agreement for "Y profil", a show of Generation Y artists from the central bank's collection; the report names Fabényi on that collection's advisory board (2025 annual report).

2026: on 3 September the central bank's new management filed a criminal complaint of suspected breach of fiduciary duty, negligent management, fraud and abuse of office over the loss of value of five properties, after an audit of MNB-Ingatlan Kft. found its real estate investments significantly overvalued (Magyar Nemzeti Bank). It is a complaint, not a charge.

Claudia Patricolo, "Why did a Hungarian museum self-censor a portrait of Viktor Orbán?" (2019)

name: Reykjavík Art Museum
overview: Municipal art museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) on three sites in central Reykjavík: Hafnarhús at Tryggvagata 17, Kjarvalsstaðir at Flókagata 24 and Ásmundarsafn at Sigtún 105; it also looks after public art in the city (museum website).

Founded in 1973; Kjarvalsstaðir, opened that year beside the Klambratún garden and named for the painter Jóhannes S. Kjarval, was the first building in Iceland designed for visual art exhibitions (Wikipedia).
Hafnarhús, a harbour warehouse of the 1930s, was renovated by Studio Grandi architects in 1998 to 2000 (Visit Reykjavík) and reopened in April 2000 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Reykjavík Art Museum: municipal: financed and managed by the City of Reykjavík
